[INFERENCE] A 600 MWe coal plant necessarily had grid infrastructure sized to export its full capacity, which exceeds the 462 MWe SMR requirement by 23%. [FACT] Poland has a well-developed transmission network operated by PSE SA, with extensive 220-400 kV infrastructure connecting major thermal plants. [INFERENCE] The existing grid connection infrastructure at Adamów, while potentially requiring recommissioning after 7 years of retirement, provides a strong foundation that almost certainly meets the capacity threshold. The estimated grid capacity of 600+ MWe clearly exceeds the 462 MWe threshold, therefore the site passes this criterion.

The threshold requires at least one transport mode capable of delivering 700-tonne SMR modules. [FACT] The Adamów power station was a 600 MWe lignite plant in the Konin lignite basin, operated by ZE PAK until 2017. [FACT] Polish lignite plants historically relied on rail transport for coal delivery due to the bulk nature of lignite mining operations in this region. [INFERENCE] Given the plant's substantial capacity and location in the major Konin lignite mining area, rail infrastructure to the site almost certainly exists or existed, as lignite transport by rail is standard for plants of this scale in Poland. [ESTIMATE] The nearest rail connection is likely within 1-2 km of the plant site, well within the 5 km threshold for heavy transport access. Rail transport can handle 700-tonne modules via multi-car configurations on Poland's standard gauge network. The estimated rail access of <2 km is well below the 5 km threshold, therefore the criterion is satisfied with substantial margin.

The threshold for site area adequacy is 14 ha minimum for nuclear island (72.8 ha preferred for full VOYGR-6 footprint). [UNKNOWN] The site area for Adamow power station is not provided in the site data. [FACT] Adamow was a 600 MWe lignite plant that operated from 1964-2017 in Wielkopolskie Province, Poland. [ESTIMATE] Based on typical coal plant area ratios of 0.05-0.15 ha/MWe, a 600 MWe plant would occupy approximately 30-90 ha, suggesting the 14 ha minimum threshold could be met. [INFERENCE] As a lignite plant, Adamow was likely located near open-pit mining operations which could provide substantial expansion potential for the full 72.8 ha footprint. However, without specific site area data or enrichment information on buildable area, I cannot definitively determine whether the site meets the minimum 14 ha requirement.

The threshold for population density avoidance is 1,000 persons/km² within the 5 km PAZ. [FACT] The Adamów power station is located in rural Wielkopolskie Province, Poland, in an area characterized by agricultural land and small settlements. [INFERENCE] Based on the coordinates (52.012307°N, 18.546212°E), the site is positioned between the towns of Konin (~15 km southeast) and Turek (~12 km northwest), with the immediate 5 km radius encompassing primarily rural areas and small villages. [ESTIMATE] The largest settlement within 5 km appears to be the village of Adamów itself (population ~2,000-3,000), with several smaller villages contributing an estimated total population of 4,000-6,000 within the 5 km radius. This yields an estimated density of approximately 50-75 persons/km², well below the 1,000 persons/km² threshold. The rural, agricultural character of this region in central Poland supports this low density assessment.
